differential.name: Hypertensive nephrosclerosis leading to end‑stage renal disease
differential.rationale: Chronic uncontrolled hypertension is the most common cause of CKD in elderly patients with severe GFR reduction and no diabetes.

differential.name: Obstructive uropathy from prostate carcinoma (post‑radical prostate cancer)
differential.rationale: Prostate cancer can cause bladder outlet obstruction and hydronephrosis, precipitating advanced renal failure in an 80‑year‑old male.

differential.name: Ischemic (vascular) nephropathy secondary to atherosclerotic disease and recent STEMI
differential.rationale: Severe atherosclerosis and recent myocardial infarction can reduce renal perfusion, contributing to CKD progression.

differential.name: Chronic interstitial nephritis from long‑term NSAID use for osteoarthritis
differential.rationale: Persistent NSAID exposure is a recognized cause of CKD in older adults with osteoarthritis.

differential.name: Acute tubular necrosis secondary to contrast exposure during recent cardiac catheterization for STEMI
differential.rationale: Contrast‑induced nephropathy can acutely worsen renal function, especially in patients with already low GFR.
